DrScientist 2026/11/24 19:28
Why? I'd contend it is based on a false premise - that secure digital comms is at the heart of crime and terrorism.

If I look at domestic terrorism events in the UK - most appear to have been done by individuals inspired by an idea rather than being part of some secret organisation held together by encrypted comms.

Likewise crime is either out of desperation, haphazard or done by people with severe problems.

Organised crime on the other hand requires both trust and fear, the sort that uses in person meetings to build and maintain.

I'd turn the 'if you have nothing to hide, why worry' argument on it's head.

If you have a reason to worry, why use digital encrption comms - when you can just meet in person or use very simple pre-agreed code phrases etc?

I accept that you can use mass surveillance to pick up suspicious behaviour of those lone terrorists ( internet history, purchase history etc ) - however such a tool in the wrong hands is much more dangerous than a few individuals in my view.
